findings.note: shardPack's chunk-bounds guard is one condition short of total. internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:686 rejects `c.ByteStart > c.ByteEnd || c.ByteEnd > len(file.Diff)` but never `c.ByteStart < 0`, so a negative ByteStart passes validation and then panics at the slice on line 709 (`files[c.Path].Diff[c.ByteStart:c.ByteEnd]`). The planner in contextprofile never emits a negative offset, so this is unreachable today, but the surrounding comment states the guard exists precisely so a malformed plan cannot persist a pack, and a panic inside the review harness is a worse failure mode than the error the guard returns for every other malformed case.

findings.note: Discover silently swallows every ReadDir error on the results directory, while its two siblings in the same file distinguish the expected one. internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:477 uses `if err == nil { ... }` with no else, so a permissions failure, an I/O error, or a results path that exists as a regular file is indistinguishable from 'nothing has been reviewed yet'. Prune (line 431) and GC (line 555) both special-case os.IsNotExist and propagate anything else. The consequence is a misleading gate: results that exist on disk are reported as absent, the manifest shows zero shards covered, and the operator is told to redo work that is already done. The direction of the failure is safe (it blocks rather than passes), which is why this is low and not medium.

evidence.note: entries, err := w.deps.ReadDir(dir); if err == nil { ... } with no error branch
GC distinguishes os.IsNotExist from a real error and returns the latter
Prune does the same, so Discover is the odd one out

findings.note: The cross-shard pack withholds the facts a cross-shard reviewer needs. crossShardPack (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:721) renders only Scope, Target, Plan hash, the shard list and the result contract; unlike shardPack it emits no Base, no Head, no Re-run section, and no path to resultsDir. Its instruction at line 737 is 'Review the integration seams across these shards using the shard results as input', but the reviewer is given neither the diff range to inspect the seams against nor the directory the shard results were written to, even though planJSON already computes resultsDir (line 627) and Header already carries Base and Head (lines 234-235). The reviewer has to reverse-engineer both from the sibling shard packs.

findings.note: The shard result contract names the shardId field without stating its required spelling, and the validator is strict about it. shardContractBody (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:667) says 'shardId' next to a file-name template of `shard-<id>.<shardHash>.result.json`, which teaches the reader that <id> is the bare '06'. But reviewmanifest requires the field itself to carry the prefix: shardIDPattern is `^shard-[0-9a-f]{1,3}(-[0-9]+)?$` (internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:60) and is asserted at line 479, so a reviewer who writes "shardId": "06" earns a 'invalid shard ID' blocker after the review work is finished. This is the same defect class resultContractFor's own comment (line 645) says it was introduced to fix for the cross-shard shape, which by contrast spells its required value out inline. Naming the exact expected value, as the pack header already does in its title, would close it.

evidence.note: shardContractBody says 'shardId' but never that it must read shard-<id>
shardIDPattern requires the shard- prefix in the field value
a mis-spelled shardId becomes a blocker on an otherwise complete review

findings.note: INSTALL.md's new sentence about the durable results directory documents only half of its lifecycle. Line 84 tells the user to commit docs/metareview/shards/ 'a later gate reads them back', but never that a later passing gate also deletes from it: GC (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:547) removes every result file in that tracked directory that does not match the current plan, and internal/prready/review.go:293 calls it on any non-blocking run. This repository currently tracks 156 files under docs/metareview/shards/, so the next passing pr-ready run will present the operator with a large batch of unexplained tracked-file deletions at exactly the moment the gate said PASS and they are about to push. The behaviour itself is deliberate and correctly gated on !result.Blocking; the gap is that the user-facing doc edited in this diff describes the directory as read-back-only.
